newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli war games end in Golan Heights.
newsitem.headline: Israeli war games end in Golan Heights.

text.p: Israeli war planes, tanks, and artillery units ended a huge military exercise in the Golan Heights on Tuesday, security sources said, amid mounting tension with neighbouring Syria.
An army spokesman described as "routine" the manoeuvres that began days ago. They follow a series of Syrian army exercises and troop movements across the border which have given Israelis war jitters.
Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara on Tuesday said Syria was not preparing for an attack on Israel and accused Israeli leaders of making the accusation to avoid making peace.
"Allegations...that Syria is escalating the situation and massing troops to launch a surprise attack are baseless," Shara said.

"Such allegations coming from the Israeli government are aimed at evading the peace process and the basis on which it was built," he told reporters at Damascus airport while seeing off his Russian counterpart Yevgeny Primakov, on a Middle East tour trying to revive to peace process.
Syria and Israel have already fought several wars and have failed in five years of sporadic peace talks to settle their dispute over the fate of the Golan Heights which Israel captured in 1967.
In September Syria redeployed some 12,000 troops in Lebanon, moving some to within striking distance of a key Israeli position on the Golan Heights.

Syria wants back all of the Golan, a high-altitude plateau, in exchange for peace. Hardline Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin who ousted a centrist Labour-led government in elections last May, has vowed to never to give up the strategic heights.

Israeli security sources said on Monday that the army had asked the government for more than $1 billion to prepare for war with Syria while Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai hinted Israel could be flexible in talks with Damascus suspended since February.

"Not one senior official in the Israeli government has said: 'Not one inch on the Golan'," an official briefing reporters quoted Mordechai as telling a parliamentary committee. The defence minister did not elaborate.

Netanyahu has called on Damascus to renew peace talks without preconditions but Syria says the negotiations must pick up where they left off. The former Labour government was prepared to make at least a partial Golan withdrawal.
"The government views the Golan Heights as necessary area for the security of the state and the preservation of its water sources," say the guidelines of Netanyahu's government established in June.
"Maintaing Israeli sovereignty over the Golan will be the foundation of any agreement with Syria," they say.
